institution: ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT Cochin)
technology_type: Food Preservation / Chemical Assays & Curing Protocols
problem_solved: Traditional fish curing relies on unscientific beach drying using low-quality, contaminated salt mixtures that trigger red halophilic bacterial infestations and rapid spoilage within two months.
description: An optimized chemical preservation methodology that mandates uniform washing filters, utilizes pure salt configurations at a standardized 1:4 salt-to-fish ratio, dries product to a moisture threshold ≤ 25%, and introduces a dusting mixture containing 3 parts calcium propionate to 27 parts powdered salt.
applications: Commercial seafood export processing plants, coastal artisanal fish curing operations, sustainable packaging facilities, food microbiology laboratories, and regional agricultural extension systems.
secondary_sector: Biotechnology & Life Sciences, Agribusiness & Rural Economy, Advanced Materials & Chemical
